title: Rav Yosef bar Manyumi
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: English translation and editorial notes prepared for Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He was a disciple of Rav Nachman, as in [Ketubot 100b](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.100b.14), where he said, “It was explained to me by Rav Nachman himself.” We repeatedly find the formula “Rav Yosef bar Manyumi said: R' Nachman said,” as in Berakhot 23a; Eruvin 45 and 76b; Yevamot 101b and 106b; Ketubot 81b; Gittin 9a, 45b and 70b; Bava Kamma 97a; Bava Metzia 15b, 32a and 64b; Bava Batra 132a, 145a, 148b and 159a; Shevuot 47; and Chullin 13b, 46a and 48a.[^1]

We also find Rav Yosef bar Manyumi saying, “Rav Sheshet said,” in [Gittin 71a](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.71a.8); and Rav Manyumi son of Rav Nachumi said it in his name, as in [Ketubot 81b](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.81b.8-11).[^2]

notes.text: The heading and literal full רב titles are retained. The exact Davidson text of Ketubot 100b:14 gives Rav Yosef bar Manyumi and Rav Nachman in the quoted explanation, resolving the personal abbreviations there. Hyman’s broader repeated formula remains his collation of the listed passages: the abbreviated Nachman in that unchecked general list stays R'. The individual list references were not all checked. Period and colon are read conventionally as a and b; Eruvin מה and Shevuot מז have no amud marker and remain 45 and 47. The ordinary tractate abbreviations are expanded as work titles, not person identifiers.

The checked Gittin 71a:8 explicitly reads Rav Yosef bar Manyumi said Rav Sheshet, supporting the expansion of ריב״מ at this exact occurrence and the direct attribution. The name is not an additional sage called “Rivam.” Ketubot 81b:8–11 names Rav Manyumi son of Rav Nachumi and then quotes the Yosef-bar-Manyumi/Nachman formula. Hyman’s “in his name” retains its unspecified antecedent; no extra teacher–student edge is inferred. His initial description as a disciple remains his historical characterization, not a newly admitted graph relationship.
